sections.label: Internet and social media figures
sections.summary: The passage lists figures showing widespread Internet and social media use, including Google searches, Facebook users, tweets and YouTube videos.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Some figures to demonstrate the widespread use of the Internet and social media are as follows: Google handles more than 5.5 billion searches each day; there are 2.27 billion monthly active users of Facebook; there are 500 million tweets which are sent each day on Twitter; and almost five billion videos are watched on YouTube every day.

sections.label: Facebook and Google Plus data exposure
sections.summary: Facebook admitted deals letting Netflix and Spotify access private messages, and Google Plus admitted exposing over 50 million users' data.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Last December, Facebook admitted that it had struck deals with companies like Netflix, Spotify, that allowed them to read, write and delete private messages of users.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Google Plus, for instance, on two separate occasions last year, admitted that it had exposed the personal data of over 50 million users in total to third-party developers.

sections.label: Cyberbullying survey and self-harm study
sections.summary: A 2017 Talking Point survey found three in four children reported cyberbullying, and a study linked it to self-harm risk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In 2017, a survey commissioned by Talking Point found that three out of four children and teenagers had reported being victims of cyberbullying.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Journal of Medical Internet Research published a study last year and showed that cyberbullying raised the risk of self-harm or suicidal behaviour amongst young persons by 2.3 times.

sections.label: ISIS-linked group publishing personnel details
sections.summary: In the US, an ISIS-linked group published names, addresses and phone numbers of 1,400 mostly military and government personnel, urging attacks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In the US, an Islamic State of Iraq and Syria-linked group published names, addresses and phone numbers of 1,400 mostly US military and government personnel, urging supporters to attack them.

sections.label: Teenager suicide after live-streamed encounter
sections.summary: In New York, an 18-year-old violinist killed himself after his roommate live-streamed him being intimate with another man to 150 people.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In New York, an 18-year-old boy, a gifted violinist, killed himself after his roommate live-streamed him behaving intimately with another man, to 150 people.

sections.label: Buying Instagram likes and retweets
sections.summary: The passage states that one million Instagram likes can be bought for US$18 and 500 retweets for US$2.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: For instance, Members will probably know that one million Instagram "likes" can be bought for US$18 and 500 retweets for US$2.

sections.label: Article shared on Facebook
sections.summary: The article was shared over 44,000 times on Facebook.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The article was shared over 44,000 times on Facebook.

sections.label: Rumours spread faster than truth
sections.summary: The study showed rumours travelled farther, faster, deeper and more broadly than truth in all categories, and Ebola falsehood tweets outnumbered corrections 2.7 to one.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The study showed that rumours travelled farther, faster, deeper and more broadly than truth in all categories of information.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The study showed that tweets which perpetrated a falsehood about the Ebola virus being transmitted by air, outnumbered tweeted corrections by 2.7 to one.

sections.label: Protection from Harassment Act amendments
sections.summary: The POHA amendments give people power to reclaim truth and dignity, simplifying recourse, clarifying remedies, and enabling action against falsehoods and harassment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) today give power to the people so that the man on the street can take back the truth and find a way to reclaim his dignity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: We seek to simplify the process to make it easier for the man on the street to get recourse, to get redress; make clear what remedies he can get; enable him to tackle falsehoods and harassment once they are published; enable him to put the truth out there, to counter falsehoods that may affect his livelihood or, in the case of a company, its business.

sections.label: Magistrate's Complaints and protection orders
sections.summary: Over 3,000 Magistrate's Complaints have been filed, with 500 protection order applications and over 200 orders granted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To date, more than 3,000 Magistrate's Complaints have been filed under the Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: There were 500 applications for protection orders under this Act, of which over 200 such orders were granted.

sections.label: Cost of applying for PO
sections.summary: Applying for a PO currently costs about $300 to $500.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Currently, applying for a PO costs about $300 to $500.

sections.label: Breach of PO not arrestable
sections.summary: At present, a breach of a PO is not arrestable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: At present, a breach of a PO is not arrestable.

sections.label: PAVE study on abusive relationships
sections.summary: A 2012 PAVE study in Singapore found one in three unmarried persons aged 15 to 34 were in an abusive relationship.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: A Promoting Alternatives to Violence (PAVE) study in 2012 in Singapore showed one in three unmarried persons between the ages of 15 and 34 were found to be in an abusive relationship.

sections.label: New Part 3A and PHC
sections.summary: The Bill has a new Part 3A which will establish the Protection from Harassment Court.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill has a new Part 3A, which will establish the Protection from Harassment Court (PHC).

sections.label: Clause 18 judge duty
sections.summary: Clause 18 imposes a duty on a judge granting the EPO to consider whether a criminal investigation is warranted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In the Bill, there is a clause 18 which imposes a duty on a judge granting the EPO to consider whether a criminal investigation is warranted.

sections.label: Clauses 16(1) and 17(1) convictions
sections.summary: Clauses 16(1) and 17(1) deem the POHA contravention requirement satisfied if the respondent was convicted of a hurt or POHA offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clauses 16(1) and 17(1) provide that if the respondent has been convicted of a hurt offence under the Penal Code, or a POHA offence, the requirement to show that the respondent has contravened POHA will be deemed satisfied.

sections.label: Clause 17 EPOs duration
sections.summary: Clause 17 will ensure EPOs remain in place until proceedings conclude unless successfully challenged.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 17 will ensure that EPOs will be in place until the conclusion of proceedings unless they are successfully challenged.

sections.label: PHC hearing timelines
sections.summary: The PHC will aim to conduct EPO hearings within 48 to 72 hours, or within 24 hours where violence is involved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The PHC will aim to conduct hearings for EPOs within 48 to 72 hours of application.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Where there is an element of violence involved, the PHC will try to conduct hearings for EPOs within 24 hours of the application.

sections.label: Court-ordered psychiatric assessment after PO
sections.summary: Clause 19 lets the Court order a respondent to undergo psychiatric assessment after a PO is granted, and treatment if criteria are met.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 19 empowers the Court to order the respondent to undergo a psychiatric assessment after it grants a PO and undergo psychiatric treatment if certain criteria are fulfilled.

sections.label: Doubled penalties for offences against vulnerable persons
sections.summary: Clause 10 doubles penalties for POHA offences against vulnerable persons, whether adults or children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Under the proposed POHA amendments, clause 10 provides that penalties for POHA offences against vulnerable persons, be they adults or children, will likewise be doubled.

sections.label: Doubled penalty for offences against intimate partners
sections.summary: Clause 11 doubles the penalty where a POHA offence is committed against an intimate partner.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In a similar vein, clause 11 of the Bill doubles the penalty if a POHA offence is committed against an intimate partner.

sections.label: Breach of PO arrestable and repeat penalties
sections.summary: Clause 22 makes PO breaches arrestable in prescribed circumstances, and clause 9(b) doubles maximum punishment for repeat breaches.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 22 provides that if a harasser breaches a PO, this will be arrestable in prescribed circumstances, such as where hurt is caused or where the harassing conduct persists despite the issuance of a PO.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In addition, clause 9(b) provides that if a harasser breaches a PO more than once, he will be liable on subsequent conviction to twice the maximum punishment prescribed.

sections.label: Doxxing offence introduced
sections.summary: Clauses 4(a) and 6(d) introduce the offence of doxxing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clauses 4(a) and 6(d) introduce the offence of doxxing.

sections.label: Take-down orders and falsehoods regime
sections.summary: The Court may order take-down of offending posts, Internet intermediary disabling, 24-hour EPO hearings, and the falsehoods regime is repealed and re-enacted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Court may order that the offending communication be taken down by the offender and persons who have shared the original post or substantially similar posts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Where appropriate, the Court may also order that an Internet intermediary disable access to the offending post.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: And finally, where an EPO involving online doxxing is involved, the Court will aim to hear the application within 24 hours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Aside from doxxing, the Bill also enhances existing measures available to address the spread of falsehoods by repealing and re-enacting the falsehoods regime.

sections.label: Falsehoods regime scope
sections.summary: Sections 15 and 16 of POHA and clause 20 of the Bill deal with false statements of fact.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: For the avoidance of doubt, the falsehoods regime under sections 15 and 16 of POHA, and clause 20 of the Bill, deals with false statements of fact.

sections.label: Five orders and interim relief
sections.summary: Clause 20 sets out five orders for false statements, with interim relief for all but the General Correction Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Once a false statement about a subject is established, clause 20 sets out five orders that may be available to address it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Interim relief will be available for all orders save the General Correction Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Interim relief can be obtained ex parte in the case of interim stop publication and interim notification orders, both of which are targeted at individuals or entities which publish falsehoods.

sections.label: Orders amended for similar statements
sections.summary: The orders have been amended to include substantially similar statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The orders have been amended to include substantially similar statements.

sections.label: Truth accessible and serious harm
sections.summary: The purpose is to make truth accessible to viewers, and orders can be made where serious harm to reputation is caused or likely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Again, the purpose of this is to ensure that where the false statement has been published by way of the Internet intermediary service, the truth is made accessible to viewers of the false statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: They can be made where the Court is satisfied that serious harm to the reputation of the subject, whether professional or otherwise, has been caused or is likely to be caused.

sections.label: Contesting claims and hearing timelines
sections.summary: Third parties may contest claims, victims can use interim relief, and the PHC aims to hear applications within set times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The third party should be allowed to fully contest the claim if it wishes to, before an order is granted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: However, a victim can still rely on other forms of interim relief to stop or stem the spread of the falsehoods, such as the disabling order or interim stop publication order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The PHC will aim to conduct hearings for the interim orders within 48 to 72 hours of application, and given the speed at which online publications can go viral, the PHC will aim to hear the application for an interim order within 24 hours of application if the false statement has been published online, subject to any requirements to give notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As with POs, the PHC will aim to hear applications for final section 15 orders within four weeks of application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In light of the decision by the Court of Appeal in AG v Ting Choon Meng, which ruled that only individual persons have recourse under section 15, clause 20 of the Bill states that both individuals and entities can apply for remedies under section 15.

sections.label: Entities seeking relief from falsehoods
sections.summary: Allowing entities to seek relief ensures companies and their staff do not suffer or lose livelihoods due to falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Allowing entities to seek relief will ensure that the companies and their staff do not suffer, lose their livelihoods, as a result of falsehoods.

sections.label: Youth cyberbullying survey findings
sections.summary: Two surveys found one in nine students and three in four youths had been cyberbullied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2014, a survey by the Singapore Children’s Society and the Institute of Mental Health of more than 3,000 students aged 12 to 17 found that one in nine had been victims of cyberbullying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2018, Channel NewsAsia's Talking Point surveyed 353 youths aged 13 to 19, finding that three in four had been cyberbullied and almost all had not informed their parents.

sections.label: Strengthened protection order provisions
sections.summary: Provisions were strengthened by extending protection to related persons, covering entities, and enhancing penalties for intimate partner or vulnerable person contraventions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Third, the other ways the provisions have been strengthened include extending the protection under POs to the person’s related to the victim, making it clear that entities can avail themselves of the protection under POHA, enhancing the penalties if a contravention of a PO was between a person and his or her intimate partner or if it was towards a vulnerable person.

sections.label: PHC expedited protection order timelines
sections.summary: The PHC aims to hear expedited protection order applications within 48 to 72 hours, or 24 hours if violence is involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Seventh, the press release says that the PHC aims to hear applications for expedited POs within 48 to 72 hours of application, with applications involving risk of violence or actual violence within 24 hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: How long does the process currently take and would the Minister share what resources will be deployed to PHC so that the suggested tight deadlines are met?

sections.label: Doxxing offence clause illustrations
sections.summary: Clause 6 clarifies factual circumstances giving rise to doxxing, though borderline cases may still pose challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, clause 6 of the Bill is helpful because it illustrates and clarifies what particular factual circumstances can operate to give rise to the offence of doxxing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, there may be a challenge in other cases, particularly borderline cases where the intent of the individual releasing identity information does not neatly cohere with the offence and illustrations in the Bill.

sections.label: Penalties for intimate relationship offences
sections.summary: Clause 11 enhances penalties for offences against intimate partners, aligning PO and EPO regimes with the Women's Charter's PPO regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My second clarification involves enhancing the penalties for offences against a victim in an intimate relationship with the offender under clause 11 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A corollary purpose of the amendments under the Bill are to bring the Protection Order (PO) and Expedited Protection Order (EPO) regime in line with the Personal Protection Order (PPO) regime under the Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe these are important amendments, providing better protection for individuals, particularly women, who may not be married but are in an intimate partner relationship and suffer from IPV at the hands of their spouses.

sections.label: Remedies for same-sex relationships
sections.summary: The question asks whether unmarried individuals in same-sex relationships can seek the Bill's proposed remedies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can I clarify if the remedies proposed under this Bill can be sought by individuals who are not married but are in same-sex relationships?

sections.label: EPO violence hearing within 24 hours
sections.summary: MinLaw indicated Courts will aim to hear EPO applications within 24 hours where there is risk of violence or actual violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, in the case of EPOs where there is a risk of violence or actual violence, the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) has indicated the Courts will aim to hear the application within 24 hours.

sections.label: Shanmugam POFMA Bill comments, entity definition
sections.summary: Shanmugam commented to Channel NewsAsia on 13 April using a bitcoin company example, and Clause 3 defines an entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Minister Shanmugam's comments on the POFMA Bill, the Minister made comments to Channel NewsAsia on 13 April and he used an actual example of the financial markets, where, I quote, "the founder of a bitcoin company had died; the news was put out deliberately by somebody, I think, seeking profit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Within a period of four or five hours, billions of dollars were wiped out from the value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lots of innocent investors lost money." Clause 3 of the Bill clarifies that an entity can seek relief under the Bill and an "entity" is defined to mean any company or association or body of persons whether corporate or incorporate.

sections.label: Costs under new section 16CA
sections.summary: The costs incurred by the applicant and claimable under the new section 16CA apply specifically to general correction orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, in view of the costs incurred by the applicant and claimable under the new section 16CA, I note these apply specifically to general correction orders.

sections.label: No PHC application against Government
sections.summary: An individual or company cannot apply to the PHCs if the Government makes misleading or false statements against them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What this effectively means is that an individual or company cannot apply to the PHCs in case the Government makes misleading or false statements against them.

sections.label: Government exemption from falsehood suits
sections.summary: The decision to exempt the Government so it cannot be sued for perpetuating a falsehood is described as a glaring omission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On this point, Mr Speaker, the decision to create an exemption for the Government such that it cannot be sued for perpetuating a falsehood is, in my view, a glaring omission and a lost opportunity at winning the trust of the public.

sections.label: No remedy against Government false statement
sections.summary: Under the Bill, such an individual would have no remedy against a false or allegedly false statement by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The limitation period of this example notwithstanding, under the Bill, such an individual would have no remedy against a false statement made by the Government, or an allegedly false statement by the Government, I should add.

sections.label: Government scrutiny and public trust
sections.summary: The speaker says information and power are asymmetric between Government and citizens, and that allowing scrutiny of falsehood accusations can strengthen trust in the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, it goes without saying that there exists an asymmetry in information and power between the Government and its citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is my view that allowing the Government to open itself up to scrutiny on matters where it is accused of peddling falsehoods can paradoxically operate to strengthen trust in the Government, particularly in these times where political leaders all around the world find their mandate to rule increasingly questioned by a sceptical public and where political polarisation increasingly appears to be the order of the day.

sections.label: POHA amendments and individual redress
sections.summary: The amended Protection from Harassment Act enhances private individuals' rights to redress for harassing online communication, though individuals should consider whether the law is the most appropriate means.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Protection from Harassment Act (POHA), with these amendments in place, will enhance the rights of private individuals to seek redress for online communication that harasses them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But individuals must also ask themselves if reference to the law is the most appropriate and effective means of solving the dispute at hand.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am not discouraging individuals or victims who receive credible threats of physical harm, or who are exposed to sustained campaigns of abuse, from using the full measure of the law against the perpetrators.

sections.label: CPF housing reform suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker suggested ending CPF use for housing and focusing CPF on retirement and medical security, and denies saying CPF funds should be locked up immediately.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Housing asset values are highly dependent on demographic conditions decades down the road, as well as on the remaining lease length.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I suggested to the reporter that a bold reform might be to end the use of CPF for housing by focusing CPF purely on retirement and medical security, which also means cutting CPF contribution rates significantly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I never said that CPF funds should be locked up immediately, so as to prevent the use of existing CPF money for housing.

sections.label: Man at university front desk
sections.summary: A gentleman turned up at the front desk of the speaker's university looking for the speaker.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: A gentleman actually turned up at the front desk of my university looking for me.

sections.label: Misconception about CPF remarks
sections.summary: The speaker realised resorting to law would not have helped anybody and had to correct a basic misconception about what was said on CPF.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: I realised that resorting to the law would not have helped anybody, least of all myself.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: There was a basic misconception about what I had said on CPF that I had to set straight.

sections.label: Straits Times and Sure Boh corrections
sections.summary: The Straits Times stood by its reporting but accepted it could be taken out of context, while Sure Boh Singapore corrected its story and publicised the correction.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: The Straits Times stood by their reporting but they accepted that what was originally printed could be taken out of context.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: Sure Boh Singapore, likewise, proved amenable to reason and corrected their story and publicised the correction.

sections.label: Facebook statement on CPF housing
sections.summary: The speaker posted a public Facebook statement on 10 May about CPF and housing and invited dialogue, without using legal rights.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: All of this was achieved without using any rights I might have under the law.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: I then posted a public statement on Facebook, on 10 May, setting out the reasons for my thinking on CPF and housing, and I invited a dialogue.

sections.label: POHA prosecutions and complaints
sections.summary: The speaker notes that since POHA came into force in November 2014, there have been over 1,700 prosecutions and over 3,000 Magistrate's Complaints.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: The law gives us rights, but justice is not always served by insisting on those rights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note that since POHA came into force in November 2014, there have been more than 1,700 prosecutions and over 3,000 Magistrate’s Complaints.

sections.label: Specialist PHC courts under POHA
sections.summary: The speaker is happy to hear that a specialist Court, the PHCs, will be established to oversee matters under POHA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, I am happy to hear that there will be an establishment of a specialist Court, the PHCs, to oversee matters under POHA.

sections.label: Offence under amended law
sections.summary: With the amendment to the law, this will be an offence and those found guilty can be fined or imprisoned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: With the amendment to the law, this will be an offence and those found guilty can be fined or imprisoned.

sections.label: Support for doxxing recommendations
sections.summary: The speaker believes doxxing goes against societal norms and fully supports the Bill's recommendations on doxxing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe that doxxing is not a good thing and goes against the norms of living as a society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, I fully support the recommendations in this Bill with respect to doxxing.

sections.label: Questions on doxxing offence and evidence
sections.summary: The speaker asks about intention, forwarding, pursuing every individual, and evidence preservation, concluding there is a need to regulate online behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: To be made an offence, there must be intention to cause harassment, alarm or distress to the target person.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: What if the individual was not the one who created the publication in the first place and was just forwarding the information?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: What if numerous people have shared and forwarded the information with malicious intent?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Will the Police and prosecutor be pursuing every individual involved?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Further, could there be possible challenges of preservation of evidence, for example, if comments or information were shared on Instagram through Insta-stories?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would be grateful for the clarification on the matters above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There is, therefore, a need to regulate behaviour online.

sections.label: Online reputations and doxxing crime
sections.summary: Speaker supports POHA amendments introducing doxxing as a crime, citing the importance of online reputations.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a digitalised world where a vast proportion of our daily interactions and transactions are undertaken online, in both professional and social realms, our online reputations are crucial to getting employed, making new friends and even finding a life partner.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, rise in support of the proposed amendments to POHA, particularly the introduction of doxxing as a crime.

sections.label: Doxxing penalties and deterrent effect
sections.summary: The amendments impose fines up to $5,000 and jail up to 12 months for doxxing, which the speaker believes deters.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the amendments, doxxing will attract stiff penalties, including fines of up to $5,000 and jail terms of up to 12 months that I believe will have a significant deterrent effect.

sections.label: Toa Payoh hawker centre misidentification
sections.summary: A 2017 viral video of a couple being rude led netizens to first identify the wrong man and woman.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In April 2017, when a video of a couple being rude to an elderly man in a Toa Payoh hawker centre went viral, netizens were quick to act but first identified the wrong man and woman.

sections.label: Questions on POHA costs and image
sections.summary: The speaker asks about online falsehood case volumes, administrative costs on intermediaries, and impact on Singapore's pro-innovation image, while supporting the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From the past records of MinLaw, what is the estimated volume of online falsehood cases that could be brought before the Courts by individuals and entities under POHA?

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How significant an administrative cost might this impose on Internet intermediaries?

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And what impact will this new regulation have on Singapore's pro-innovation image?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Speaker, I rise in support of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill, if passed, would strengthen and streamline the protection from harassment as well as fake news.

sections.label: False claims about chin chow and Bata
sections.summary: A false plastic claim about Tan Soon Mui's chin chow was disproven, and Bata Malaysia lost over half a million ringgit to fake news.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, two years ago, a man made a claim online that a grass-jelly or chin chow product manufactured locally by Tan Soon Mui Food Industries is made of plastic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: That video was widely shared on social media but proven false two weeks later by the Agri-Food and Veterinary Authority after it conducted laboratory tests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Also in 2017, shoe company Bata in Malaysia lost more than half a million ringgit within a month after fake news about it selling shoes with the Arabic word "Allah" forming on the soles went viral.

sections.label: PHC powers and victim damages
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether fake news victims can piggy-back on criminal investigations and whether the PHC can award damages without a civil suit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Another point, regarding the establishment of the PHC which has the powers to hear both criminal and civil matters, I would like to ask: in practice, does it mean that a victim of fake news would only need to make a Police report and the victim would be then able to "piggy-back" on the criminal investigations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In terms of damages suffered by the victim, would PHC be able to award damages to the victim without the victim bringing a civil suit if it has already been established by the Court that the perpetrator has, indeed, committed an offence and caused damage to the victim?

sections.label: Streamlining POHA order applications
sections.summary: Section 17 of the Bill streamlines applying for POHA orders, which currently require a lawyer costing $5,000 to $8,000 before mediation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One major change introduced is streamlining the process for applying and obtaining POHA orders in section 17 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, applicants need a lawyer to assist in the preparation and submission of documents and subsequent proceedings and this can be financially prohibitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It typically costs between $5,000 and $8,000 leading up to mediation, and significantly higher if mediation fails and the matter goes to Court.

sections.label: EPO application timelines
sections.summary: The Minister said subsidiary legislation will stipulate EPO applications under POHA could be granted within 48 to 72 hours, or 24 hours if violence or risk of violence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Though not provided for in the primary legislation, the Minister has assured us in his statements to the media that the subsidiary legislation will stipulate that an EPO application under POHA could be granted within 48 to 72 hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If there is actual violence or risk of violence, an EPO could be granted within 24 hours.

sections.label: Enhanced penalties for vulnerable persons
sections.summary: Section 8 of the Bill introduces enhanced penalties for perpetrators for crimes against vulnerable persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The other significant change introduced in section 8 of the Bill is close to my heart, namely, enhanced penalties for perpetrators for crimes against vulnerable persons.

sections.label: Victim support over harsh punishment
sections.summary: The passage argues harsh punishments are not necessarily effective deterrents, and CEDAW suggested Singapore prioritise gender sensitisation training in the criminal justice system instead of increasing punishments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Harsh punishments are not necessarily an effective deterrent nor do they serve survivors better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Instead, increasing victim support and making reporting and prosecution processes trauma-informed and more victim-friendly would go a long way in ensuring that survivors will come forward and sustain their involvement all the way to conviction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Improving the chances of securing convictions will do more to promote deterrence than imposing harsh penalties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CEDAW suggested that Singapore prioritises gender sensitisation training in the criminal justice system, not increasing punishments, as a way to strengthen protection for women against gender-based violence.

sections.label: Mandatory harassment code for IHLs
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to consider a mandatory code on sexual and other harassment to hold IHLs accountable for handling student complaints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If they are not covered, I strongly urge the Government to consider establishing a mandatory code on sexual and other forms of harassment that can hold IHLs accountable when they do not handle student complaints promptly and fairly.

sections.label: Criminalising publishing identifying information
sections.summary: The Bill criminalises publishing online identifying information of others, such as full name, address and phone number.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In English): This Bill criminalises publishing online identifying information of others, such as full name, address, phone number and so on.

sections.label: Wrongly identified bank employees doxxed
sections.summary: Netizens wrongly identified a couple in a viral bullying video as bank employees and threatened to boycott the bank.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When netizens tried to identify the perpetrators in a viral video of a young couple bullying an elderly man at Toa Payoh Hawker Centre, they wrongly identified them to be employees of a local bank.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This information, along with the couple’s pictures, were circulated, and people even threatened to boycott the bank.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Eventually, it was found to be a mistake.

sections.label: Resident's post-resignation harassment complaint
sections.summary: A resident says her ex-boss kept contacting her and circulated her contract after she resigned, and asks if this is harassment.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Her ex-boss said, "I agree to your resignation, but I disagree to you resigning without giving notice.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to her, in her employment contract, during the probation period, she needs to give only one week's notice.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, she has been bombarded with WhatsApp, email messages and even her personal details and her employment contract was circulated to her ex-colleagues.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Her boss told her that he is taking legal action on her and, in order to do that, he had to deliver a notice to her personally and kept asking her when he could visit her at home.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mind you, she has left the company for six months.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State if this is harassment.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can this Bill help a victim like my resident?

sections.label: Sharing personal data to humiliate
sections.summary: Publicly sharing personally identifiable information while inciting people to punish or humiliate targeted parties has become increasingly common.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Publicly sharing personally identifiable information, such as photographs, videos, addresses, phone and contact details, while inciting people to "punish" or humiliate targeted parties have become increasingly common.

sections.label: Doxxing harms innocent families
sections.summary: The passage states that taking the law into one's own hands, especially doxxing, can cause unnecessary harm to the parties and their innocent families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We should not encourage violence in our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And one taking the law into one's own hands, especially doxxing, can cause unnecessary harm to the parties concerned, including their families, who are innocent parties.

sections.label: Threats of violence and online manipulation
sections.summary: The passage says threats of violence should not be dealt with lightly and that the public could be used for mass manipulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The damage and harm are far-reaching and hurt the children who are the innocent parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Therefore, anyone who advocates and resorts to all means to hunt down another party with threats of violence should not be dealt with lightly as such threats are provocations to violent behavior, which are against the efforts to make Singapore a gracious society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We should also educate the public and raise awareness that they could be used for mass manipulation by persons with their own agendas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There are already cases of companies and individuals misleading the public online with information discrediting their business rivals in order to gain a competitive advantage in their businesses and improve their own profits.

sections.label: PHC protection for harassment victims
sections.summary: The PHC's simplified procedures and expedited timelines, with stronger victim protection, signal that harassment cases must be dealt with effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The establishment of the PHC which adopts simplified procedures and expedited timelines, coupled with the strengthening of protection for victims of harassment, sends a strong signal that victims of harassment must be taken seriously, and harassment cases must be dealt with effectively.

sections.label: Intimate harasser exception proof
sections.summary: The Bill gives stronger protection to victims of intimate harassers but exempts harassers who prove the relationship did not affect the victim's ability to protect themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Bill rightly provides for strengthened protection for victims of intimate harassers who require greater protection and means to extricate themselves from the reach of the intimate harasser.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, the Bill also provides that the enhanced penalties do not apply to the intimate harasser, referred to as "A", if "A" can prove that despite "A" having been or being in an intimate relationship with the victim, referred to as "B", the relationship between "A" and "B" did not adversely affect "B's" ability to protect "B" from "A" in respect of the harm caused by the offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share examples of what these possible exceptions might be?

sections.label: Review of public service scope
sections.summary: The member repeats a call for MinLaw and MHA to review the scope of public service workers under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Following this incident, I reiterate my call once again for MinLaw and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to review the scope of "public service" workers under the Act.

sections.label: Colleague's photos and untruths
sections.summary: A member shared that a colleague with a grudge took her photographs without consent and spread malicious untruths about an intimate relationship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: A member shared that her colleague who bore a grudge against her took photographs of her without her consent and spread malicious untruths about her, suggesting that she was in an intimate relationship with another colleague.

sections.label: Superior's false allegations after report
sections.summary: A member shared that after she reported her superior for workplace sexual harassment, he made false allegations, removed her duties and dismissed her.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: One member shared that after she had made a Police report against her superior for sexual harassment at the workplace, her superior subsequently made false allegations against her, took away her work duties and dismissed her.

sections.label: Business entities and falsehood orders
sections.summary: The Bill lets business entities seek stop publication and correction orders against falsehoods, such as videos about fake chilli and fake keropok.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: On a related note, the Bill allows business entities to seek relief against falsehoods through the application of stop publication and correction orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Last year, videos were circulated alleging that fake chilli was sold in the vicinity of Tekka Market and fake keropok was sold at the Hari Raya Bazaar.

sections.label: Broadened civil action against entities
sections.summary: The member says people should know what behaviour is caught, and proposed section 11 lets harassment victims bring civil action against individuals or entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I think it is important to understand what kind of behaviour would be caught under this new provision so that people will know how they should regulate their conduct online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I now turn to the proposed section 11 which is being broadened to allow for a victim of harassment to bring civil action against any individual or entity, and this entity may include corporate bodies or unincorporated bodies.

sections.label: Employer suing harasser for employees
sections.summary: Section 11 of POHA gives harassed employees a civil remedy, but it is unclear whether their employer can sue to protect them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under section 11 of POHA, clearly, the harassed employees will have a remedy in commencing civil action against the harasser.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, it is not clear to me whether the company, the employer of the employees, would be able to commence an action to protect its employees.

sections.label: UK employer suing harasser precedent
sections.summary: In the United Kingdom, precedent allows an employer to sue a harasser on behalf of all its employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the United Kingdom (UK), there is precedent that allows an employer to sue a harasser on behalf of all its employees.

sections.label: Victims demanding return of videos
sections.summary: It is unclear whether under the proposed provision victims can demand that respondents give back videos featuring them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What is not clear, though, is whether under the proposed provision, the victims are able to demand that the respondents give back the videos featuring them.

sections.label: Double actionability and overseas defamation
sections.summary: Under the common law double actionability rule, a person defamed overseas may in certain circumstances commence action in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under common law, there is a "double actionability" rule which the Senior Minister of State would know.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, a person who has been defamed overseas may, in certain circumstances, commence an action in Singapore if he can show that the offending act that occurred overseas would constitute a civil wrong both at the location where it had occurred as well as Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In an interconnected world, these kinds of expanded bases of jurisdictions would be welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Otherwise, the victims would be left with no remedy and has to wait until he or she is harassed in Singapore before commencing action.

sections.label: Harassment victims' time and PO concerns
sections.summary: PHC will adopt simplified procedures and expedite hearings, including within 48 to 72 hours for EPOs and 24 hours where violence risk exists.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Two of the main concerns of harassment victims are the time required and also difficulties faced in getting POs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am heartened to note that PHC will adopt simplified procedures and expedite the hearings for certain applications, for example, within 48 to 72 hours for EPOs, and where there is risk of violence or violence had already occurred, within 24 hours.

sections.label: Community orders and arrestable breaches
sections.summary: The measures include community orders and making breaches arrestable offences in cases of causing hurt or continued harassment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The measures include the issuance of community orders and, in the cases of causing hurt or continued harassment, making such breaches arrestable offences.

sections.label: Effectiveness data on POs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will share recent data on PO effectiveness, including repeated breaches, injuries or deaths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry also share recent data on the effectiveness of POs, including the number of cases of repeated breaches or subsequent injuries or perhaps even deaths?

sections.label: Doxxing awareness and public education
sections.summary: The passage urges the Ministry to raise awareness of doxxing as an illegal act and of measures the public can take.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In fact, there have been many cases where false or misleading information had been shared, causing hurt and damage to innocent parties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to step up awareness of what constitutes the illegal act of doxxing through public education programmes as well as the appropriate measures the man in the street can take to address bad social behaviours.

sections.label: Bill, harassment redress and doxxing
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill makes it easier for victims to seek redress and targets doxxing and fake news.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As it has often been said, not only should justice be done, it must be seen to be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill will amplify these positive effects by making it easier for victims to seek redress and recourse for harassment-related behaviours and by targeting new social trends, such as doxxing and increasing incidences of fake news.

sections.label: Arrestable breaches of POs, EPOs
sections.summary: The passage says the amendments make certain breaches of POs and EPOs arrestable offences to give victims quicker relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, I am heartened that the amendments in this Bill seek to provide quicker relief for victims of harassment by making certain breaches of POs and EPOs arrestable offences.

sections.label: Social worker for PO, EPO cases
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister will look into attaching a social worker once a PO or EPO is issued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While the PPO operates in a separate regime under the Women’s Charter, harassment victims who obtain a PO or EPO under POHA might find themselves in similar threatening situations with the harasser.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, will the Minister look into immediately attaching a social worker to such cases once a PO or EPO has been issued?

sections.label: Mandatory counselling and mediation consideration
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister will consider requiring the Court to consider counselling and mediation and order it where appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider making it a mandatory requirement that the Court consider referring counselling and mediation options for parties, and making such an order where appropriate?

sections.label: Prohibition on revealing identity information
sections.summary: It asks whether there should be a bright-line prohibition on revealing sensitive identity information like NRIC, passport numbers, addresses and phone numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, regardless of intent, should there be a bright-line prohibition on revealing certain categories of identity information, such as National Registration Identity Card numbers, passport numbers, addresses and phone numbers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These categories of information are very sensitive and anyone who publishes this information must reasonably know of the risk that the information may be abused by the public in ways that might cause the individual harassment, alarm or distress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding that the publisher did not expressly or specifically intend to do so, he or she should be taken to have acted in willful disregard of the risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The nature of these categories of information mean that they can be misused for nefarious purposes with particularly devastating consequences for the individual.

sections.label: Applications for POs by minors
sections.summary: It notes a suggestion to let 16 to 21 year olds apply for POs without parents, and cites clause 24 allowing prescribed third parties to bring proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ms Anthea Ong has suggested to allow persons between 16 and 21 years of age to make applications for POs without their parents or legal guardians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We recognise that, in some cases, there are groups of victims who require assistance in seeking legal redress, and for their own reasons, may not want parents to be involved or to be aware of it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is why clause 24 of the Bill permits prescribed third parties, such as voluntary welfare organisations, to bring civil proceedings on behalf of a victim.

sections.label: Court officers at Harassment Cases Registry
sections.summary: It states that Court officers at the Harassment Cases Registry already explain processes under POHA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Currently, there are already Court officers at the Harassment Cases Registry to explain the processes under POHA.

sections.label: Law students giving pro bono help
sections.summary: It states that law students are available pro bono onsite to give general advice, help with form filling and draft affidavits in complicated cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On top of this, on a pro bono basis, law students are available to assist onsite to provide general advice to help with the form filling and also, in the case of more complicated factually involved cases, to assist in the drafting of affidavits in the application.

sections.label: Timelines for PO and EPO hearings
sections.summary: It sets out timelines: pretrial conference three to four weeks after filing, final PO hearing within four weeks, and EPO hearing within three working days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Currently, an application for a PO is fixed for a pretrial conference about three to four weeks after the applicant's Originating Summons and Affidavit are filed and processed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The hearing for the final PO is generally fixed within four weeks from the last pretrial conference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Applications for EPOs are fixed for a hearing before a judge within three working days from the date these documents are filed.

sections.label: Arrestable breaches of POs
sections.summary: It states that the first deterrent measure is to make breaches of POs arrestable in prescribed circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The first deterrent measure is to make breaches of POs arrestable in prescribed circumstances.

sections.label: Proof victim's protection unaffected
sections.summary: If the accused proves the victim's ability to protect himself was not adversely affected by their relationship, enhanced penalties do not apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If the accused person can prove that the victim's ability to protect himself or herself from the accused was not adversely affected by reason of their relationship, then the enhanced penalties will not apply.

sections.label: POHA protection orders statistics
sections.summary: Since POHA came into force on 15 November 2014, 406 POs and EPOs were made and 51 Magistrate's Complaints filed for alleged breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Since POHA came into force on 15 November 2014, 406 POs and EPOs have been made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In the same period, 51 Magistrate's Complaints have been filed for alleged breaches of POs and EPOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In six out of these 51 cases, there was a breach of a PO or an EPO on more than one occasion.

sections.label: POHA section 3 offence
sections.summary: Section 3 of POHA makes it an offence to target a person and cause another person harassment, alarm or distress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The starting point is section 3 of POHA which makes it an offence to target a person, which can include a company, and cause any other person, which can also include the company’s employees, to suffer harassment, alarm or distress.

sections.label: PHC damages without civil suit
sections.summary: Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked whether the PHC may award damages to a victim of a false statement without a civil suit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First, Mr Yee Chia Hsing has asked whether the PHC may award damages to a victim of a false statement without the victim bringing a civil suit.

sections.label: Remedies supplement civil actions
sections.summary: These remedies supplement existing civil actions for defamation and malicious falsehoods, and clause 20 allows related civil proceedings in PHC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These remedies are intended to supplement and not replace the existing civil actions for defamation and malicious falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: However, clause 20 of the Bill allows the victim of a falsehood to commence related civil proceedings in PHC.

sections.label: Harm not limited to physical
sections.summary: Mr Christopher de Souza asked whether harm in section 16AA is limited to physical harm, and the answer is no.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked further whether the word "harm" in section 16AA is limited to physical harm and the answer is no.

sections.label: Courts handling more cases
sections.summary: The Courts are equipped to deal with any increase in the number of cases brought.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the first point, the Courts are equipped to deal with any increase in the number of cases brought.

sections.label: Intermediaries under POHA orders
sections.summary: Intermediaries are not newly brought within POHA, as POs and section 15 orders can already be made against them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, it is not a new amendment to bring these intermediaries within POHA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And the starting point is that POs as well as orders under section 15 can today already be made against these intermediaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Given this, we do not expect that the revised regime will impose significant additional administrative cost on these platforms.

sections.label: Identifying anonymous respondents or publishers
sections.summary: POHA allows anonymous respondents or publishers to be identified by Internet location address, website, username, account, email address or other unique identifier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: POHA currently provides that where the respondent or publisher is anonymous, they may be identified by an Internet location address, a website, a username, an account or an email address, or any other unique identifier as the Court may order.

sections.label: Preserving disappearing offensive content
sections.summary: A victim or acquaintances can screenshot offensive content that disappears to preserve it as evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For example, if a victim or a victim's acquaintances come across offensive content on such platforms which disappear after a certain period of time, he or she can take a screenshot and try and preserve the nature of the content so that that can be used subsequently as evidence.

sections.label: Information identifying an individual
sections.summary: It could be, since it is information that can, alone or with other information, identify an individual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The answer is yes, it could, since it is information that can, on its own or possibly with other information, identify an individual.

sections.label: Defence of reasonableness in Bill
sections.summary: The Bill provides a defence of reasonableness, so a person who proves his conduct was reasonable will not be guilty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The law provides in the Bill for a defence of reasonableness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This means that if a person can prove that his conduct was reasonable, he will not be guilty of the offences.

sections.label: Opinions and social debate excluded
sections.summary: Posts stating opinions or encouraging social debate do not fall within the offences, and queries over conduct without intent to harass are not covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is really a question of trying to show that you might have some queries over the conduct, but there is not otherwise, from the Member's example, an intention to cause harassment to this individual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I would add that posts which merely state opinions or which are meant to encourage social debate, for example, do not fall within the ambit of offences.

sections.label: Court assesses harassment intention
sections.summary: Prosecution requires intention to cause harassment to be proven beyond reasonable doubt, and cases are too fact-specific for guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But we want the Court to be able to look at each fact, look at each case, understand the context and circumstances in which it is done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And bear in mind that for a person to be prosecuted under this offence, it has to be established beyond any reasonable doubt that the intention of the posting or the publication was to cause the harassment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I mentioned, because it is very heavily fact-specific, it may not be meaningful to set them out into a set of compendium of guidelines to try to guide each case.

sections.label: Government bound by legislation
sections.summary: The Government is not bound by legislation unless the legislation expressly provides that it is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The general position in law is that the Government is not bound by legislation unless it expressly provides for that to be so.

sections.label: Misleading statements are statements of fact
sections.summary: A misleading statement is a statement of fact, while the Member's cited example is a view outside the Bill's realm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: A misleading statement is still a statement of fact and is not a comment or an opinion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The example the Member cited, "May commit violence if you attend a black metal band concert" is a view that has been formed, is a culmination of various factors which have led a person to come to that conclusion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is not a statement of fact, nor can it be categorised as a misleading statement, which is also a statement of fact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, that statement that the Member has cited is outside of the realm of this Bill.

sections.label: POHA applies to statements of fact
sections.summary: If something is not a statement of fact, POHA does not apply to it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: No, if it is not a statement of fact, then POHA does not apply.
